steps.do: For each dispute, check the per-dispute provisional credit criteria. (a) The card account's date opened (read_accounts) is at least 60 days before today (get_time). (b) The reason is 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge' or 'duplicate_charge', or it is 'goods_services_not_received' with a purchase date (read_transactions) more than 30 days before today (get_time). (c) The amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the tier maximum of the card the transaction is on: Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards, Crypto-Cash Back) $2500.00; Mid Tier (Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom) $5000.00; Premium Tier (Gold Rewards, Business Gold Rewards) $10000.00; Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards, Business Platinum Rewards) $15000.00; Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite) $25000.00. (d) For any reason other than 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge', contacted_merchant is true. A dispute that fails any of these is not eligible. 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging' and 'refund_never_processed' are never eligible. The fourth criterion, the dispute count, is applied at filing (order_by_dispute_limit, file_dispute).

tools.not_used: Not used to post provisional credit. Its document covers goodwill, promotional, fee and other account credits. Its only dispute reason is 'dispute_resolution': Credit issued as part of dispute resolution, which means a resolved dispute, not a provisional one. Provisional eligibility goes to the dispute tool as eligible_for_provisional_credit. No document tells the agent to post provisional credit by hand.

info.about: At least two of: date of birth, email, phone number, address (plus the name or email used to look up the record)

info.about: For each charge: the card it is on, merchant, amount and date

info.about: What went wrong with each charge, mapped to one dispute_reason value

steps.do: Have the customer list every charge to dispute, card by card. Match each one to a transaction in read_transactions by card, merchant, amount and date, and record its transaction_id, purchase date (MM/DD/YYYY), amount and card account. If a charge cannot be found, tell the customer and ask them to check the details. If read_dispute_history already shows a dispute for that transaction_id, tell the customer it is already disputed and do not file it again. For a duplicate charge, show the customer the matching charges and ask which one is the duplicate to dispute.
steps.quote: transaction_id (string) - ID of the transaction being disputed.

basis.clause: match each charge to its transaction_id
basis.quote: transaction_id (string) - ID of the transaction being disputed.

basis.clause: do not refile a transaction that is already disputed
basis.quote: Use status to determine whether action is needed.

basis.clause: for a duplicate, ask which of the matching charges to dispute
basis.why: Credit card documents give no rule for which of two duplicate charges to dispute. The debit rule ('Dispute the earliest') applies only to debit card disputes.

steps.do: For each charge on its own, ask what happened. Set dispute_reason to the one value whose definition fits: 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge' (not authorized or fraudulent), 'duplicate_charge' (same charge appeared multiple times), 'incorrect_amount' (amount charged differs from expected), 'goods_services_not_received' (never received what was paid for), 'goods_services_not_as_described' (received item/service differs from description), 'canceled_subscription_still_charging' (subscription cancelled but charges continue), 'refund_never_processed' (merchant promised refund but it was never applied).
steps.quote: dispute_reason (string) - Ask user to select one. Must be exactly one of these values:

basis.clause: ask the user to select one reason per charge
basis.quote: dispute_reason (string) - Ask user to select one. Must be exactly one of these values:
'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge': Charge was not authorized or is fraudulent
'duplicate_charge': Same charge appeared multiple times
'incorrect_amount': Amount charged differs from expected
'goods_services_not_received': Never received what was paid for
'goods_services_not_as_described': Received item/service differs from description
'canceled_subscription_still_charging': Subscription was cancelled but charges continue
'refund_never_processed': Merchant promised refund but it was never applied

steps.do: For each charge on its own, ask whether the customer tried to resolve it with the merchant first. Record true or false. Ask this for fraud charges too, because the parameter is required, but do not require merchant contact before filing a fraud dispute.
steps.quote: contacted_merchant (boolean) - Ask user: Did you try to resolve this with the merchant first? Pass true or false

basis.quote: contacted_merchant (boolean) - Ask user: Did you try to resolve this with the merchant first? Pass true or false

basis.clause: fraud does not need merchant contact
basis.quote: However, if you've already tried contacting the merchant without success, or if the charge appears to be fraudulent, please don't hesitate to reach out to us right away.

steps.do: For each charge on its own, ask which resolution the customer wants. The tool accepts only 'full_refund' (complete refund of the transaction amount) and 'partial_refund' (partial amount). When only part of the charge is in dispute (for example an overcharge, or a partial refund the merchant promised), partial_refund fits: partial_refund_amount is the disputed part the customer states, such as the amount charged minus the correct amount, or the promised refund amount. When the whole charge is in dispute, full_refund fits. Do not offer 'reversal_of_charge', because the tool does not accept it.
steps.quote: resolution_requested (string) - Ask user what resolution they want. Must be exactly one of these values:

basis.quote: resolution_requested (string) - Ask user what resolution they want. Must be exactly one of these values:
'full_refund': Complete refund of the transaction amount
'partial_refund': Partial amount (must also provide partial_refund_amount)

basis.clause: partial amount is a dollar figure
basis.quote: partial_refund_amount (number, optional) - Only required if resolution_requested is 'partial_refund'. The dollar amount for the partial refund.

basis.why: Doc 014 lists 'reversal_of_charge', but the tool description says resolution_requested 'Must be one of: 'full_refund', 'partial_refund''. The tool decides its values.

steps.do: Ask when the customer noticed each issue. Use the date they give, in MM/DD/YYYY. If they say today, use today's date from get_time. Never guess a date.
steps.quote: issue_noticed_date (string, format MM/DD/YYYY) - Ask user when they noticed the issue.

steps.do: For each card with charges being disputed, ask whether the customer wants to keep the card active or have it cancelled and replaced. Record 'keep_active' or 'cancel_and_reissue' for every dispute on that card.

steps.do: For each dispute, check the per-dispute provisional credit criteria. (a) The card account's date opened (read_accounts) is at least 60 days before today (get_time). (b) The reason is 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge' or 'duplicate_charge', or it is 'goods_services_not_received' with a purchase date more than 30 days before today. (c) The amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the card tier's maximum: Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards, Crypto-Cash Back) $2500.00; Mid Tier (Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom) $5000.00; Premium Tier (Gold Rewards, Business Gold Rewards) $10000.00; Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards, Business Platinum Rewards) $15000.00; Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite) $25000.00. (d) For any reason other than 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge', contacted_merchant is true. A dispute that fails any of these is not eligible: 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging' and 'refund_never_processed' are never eligible.
steps.quote: eligible_for_provisional_credit (boolean) - Agent must determine this based on the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines article in this knowledge base. Pass true or false.

basis.quote: 1. Account Standing: The customer's credit card account has been open for at least 60 days
2. Dispute Reason Category: The dispute reason is one of the following:

basis.clause: not received only after 30 days from purchase
basis.quote: 'goods_services_not_received' (only if purchase was made more than 30 days ago)
3. Dispute Amount: The transaction amount must be at least $25.00 and must not exceed the card's maximum provisional credit limit based on card tier (see below)
Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00
Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00
Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00
Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card): Maximum $15000.00
Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite Card): Maximum $25000.00
5. Contacted Merchant: For non-fraud disputes (anything other than 'unauthorized_fraudulent_charge'), the customer must have attempted to resolve with the merchant first
Dispute reason is 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging', or 'refund_never_processed'

steps.do: Count the disputes in read_dispute_history whose submission date is within the 12 months before today (get_time). Provisional credit also needs the customer to have filed no more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months, and every dispute filed in this conversation adds to that count. So if more disputes would pass decide_eligibility_inputs than the remaining count allows, tell the customer that provisional credit is limited by the number of disputes filed and ask which charges to file first. File in the order the customer chooses, putting the ones they prioritize first.

steps.do: After each filing, act on the reply. On 'Error: Dispute may have already been filed for this transaction', tell the customer it is already disputed and do not file it again (it still counts toward the 12-month dispute count if it is in the history). On a missing or invalid parameter error, correct the value from the steps above and retry once. If a system error stops filing, ask the customer whether they want a transfer. If they agree, call transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'technical_system_error' and a summary of the disputes filed and those not yet filed.

steps.do: Tell the customer, for each charge, whether the dispute was filed and whether provisional credit applies. If it does not, give the reason in general terms: reason type, under $25.00 or over the tier maximum, merchant not contacted, purchase within 30 days, account under 60 days, or dispute count. Also say that the case will be reviewed within 10 business days.
steps.quote: When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

rules.rule: Provisional credit is true only if all of these hold: the account has been open 60 days or more; the reason is fraud or duplicate, or not received with a purchase more than 30 days ago; the amount is from $25.00 up to the tier maximum; no more than 2 disputes were filed in the past 12 months; and, for a non-fraud dispute, the merchant was contacted.
rules.quote: Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true:

rules.rule: The tier maximum is the tier's own figure (Entry $2500.00, Mid $5000.00, Premium $10000.00, Elite $15000.00, Invitation $25000.00). Crypto-Cash Back and EcoCard are Entry; Gold Rewards and Business Gold Rewards are Premium.
